title: 2 Things You Didn't Know About the Hennessey Venom F5

scenes.text: The Hennessey Venom F5 is named after a tornado, and its headline horsepower depends on what you pour into the tank. Those are two things most people do not know about America's most extreme hypercar, and a third thing sits behind both of them: the car has never yet shown the three hundred mile per hour top speed it was built to chase. Here are the facts, with every figure sourced.
scenes.caption: 2 THINGS YOU DIDN'T KNOW ABOUT THE HENNESSEY VENOM F5

scenes.text: This is the first video in a series on the Venom F5 and its rival, the SSC Tuatara. We will cover the name, the power figures, the production run, the sticker price, the test results, and a crash. We read Wikipedia, evo, The Drive and Motor One. When two numbers disagree, we show both. And where a number is our own arithmetic, we say so.
scenes.caption: SOURCES: WIKIPEDIA · EVO · THE DRIVE · MOTOR1 · OUR ARITHMETIC IS LABELLED

scenes.text: Secret one. Wikipedia says the F5 in the name refers to the top rating on the Fujita scale, the scale for tornado intensity. An F5 tornado has winds of two hundred sixty-one to three hundred eighteen miles per hour, or four hundred twenty to five hundred twelve kilometres per hour. So the name is not a model number, it is a wind speed.
scenes.caption: F5 = TOP OF THE FUJITA SCALE · WINDS 261–318 MPH (420–512 KM/H) (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: Look at the numbers side by side. The lowest F5 wind is two hundred sixty-one miles per hour. The highest is three hundred eighteen. Hennessey's stated goal, according to Wikipedia, is a top speed above three hundred eleven miles per hour, which is five hundred kilometres per hour. By our arithmetic, that sits inside the F5 wind band, about fifty miles per hour above its lower edge.
scenes.query: Hennessey Venom F5 top speed goal
scenes.caption: GOAL 311 MPH IS INSIDE THE 261–318 MPH F5 BAND, ~50 MPH ABOVE ITS LOWER EDGE (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Hennessey Special Vehicles was established in twenty seventeen, Wikipedia says, and builds the car in Sealy, Texas, at Hennessey Performance Engineering. The designer was Nathan Malinick. Development was contracted to Delta Motorsport of Silverstone, England, which also built the previous Venom GT cars. So the tornado name sits on a Texas car with an English engineering partner.
scenes.caption: HENNESSEY SPECIAL VEHICLES EST. 2017 · SEALY, TEXAS · DESIGNER NATHAN MALINICK · DELTA MOTORSPORT, SILVERSTONE (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: The F5 replaced the Venom GT. Wikipedia says the Venom GT was built on the Lotus Elise and Exige platform, though Hennessey is not associated with Lotus Cars. The Venom GT recorded two hundred seventy point four nine miles per hour at the Kennedy Space Center on the fourteenth of February, twenty fourteen, in one direction over a limited distance. The successor was unveiled in November twenty seventeen.
scenes.caption: VENOM GT: 270.49 MPH, FEB 14, 2014, ONE DIRECTION (WIKIPEDIA) · F5 UNVEILED NOV 2017

scenes.text: Why did that run not count as a world record? Wikipedia gives two reasons: it was one direction only, and only twenty-nine cars were built to the Guinness rule, which needs at least thirty for a production car record. So the F5's story starts with an almost-record. That history helps explain why the F5 is a clean-sheet car and why its builders talk so much about verification.
scenes.caption: VENOM GT RUN NOT RECOGNISED: ONE-WAY ONLY · 29 CARS vs 30 REQUIRED (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: Secret two. The F5's famous power figure is not one number. Wikipedia lists the six point six litre twin-turbo Fury V8 at one thousand eight hundred seventeen horsepower and eleven hundred ninety-three pound-feet of torque. Then it adds that on ninety-one octane, the rating is one thousand five hundred forty-two horsepower. The headline figure needs a different fuel.
scenes.caption: 1,817 HP / 1,193 LB-FT · ON 91 OCTANE: 1,542 HP (WIKIPEDIA)
scenes.chapter: Secret two: the number depends on the fuel

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the gap is two hundred seventy-five horsepower, which is about fifteen percent of the headline number. So a buyer who fills the car with ordinary premium pump fuel does not get what the poster says. The page does not say which fuel gives the headline figure. We would rather tell you that than guess, so check the exact fuel with Hennessey before quoting it.
scenes.caption: 1,817 − 1,542 = 275 HP (15.1% OF THE HEADLINE) (OUR ARITHMETIC) · FUEL FOR THE HEADLINE FIGURE: NOT STATED

scenes.text: The Evolution package makes the fuel point explicit. Wikipedia says it was released in April twenty twenty-five, costs an extra two hundred eighty-five thousand dollars, and raises output on E eighty-five to two thousand thirty-one horsepower and fourteen hundred forty-five pound-feet. The claimed zero to two hundred miles per hour time is ten point three seconds. Here the fuel is named, E eighty-five.
scenes.caption: EVOLUTION (APRIL 2025): +$285,000 · 2,031 HP / 1,445 LB-FT ON E85 · 0–200 MPH CLAIMED 10.3 s (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: The magazine evo reviewed the Evolution in June twenty twenty-five and gives two thousand thirty-one brake horsepower at eight thousand rpm, up two hundred fourteen on the regular F5. By our arithmetic, one thousand eight hundred seventeen plus two hundred fourteen is two thousand thirty-one, so evo and Wikipedia agree. That is an eleven point eight percent increase over the headline figure, and thirty-one point seven percent over the ninety-one octane figure.
scenes.query: evo Hennessey Venom F5 Evolution review
scenes.caption: evo: 2,031 BHP AT 8,000 RPM, +214 · 1,817 + 214 = 2,031 · +11.8% vs HEADLINE · +31.7% vs 91-OCTANE (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Wikipedia also gives a power-to-weight number: one thousand three hundred fifty-eight horsepower per ton. Check it by our arithmetic. One thousand eight hundred seventeen divided by the reported weight with fluids, one thousand three hundred thirty-eight kilograms, gives about one thousand three hundred fifty-eight per metric tonne. So the figure is per metric tonne, not per short ton, which a casual reader would not know.
scenes.query: Hennessey Venom F5 power to weight
scenes.caption: 1,817 HP ÷ 1.338 t ≈ 1,358 HP PER METRIC TONNE (WIKIPEDIA FIGURE, OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: There is a small oddity in the weight figures. Wikipedia lists a curb weight of three thousand fifty-three pounds, or one thousand three hundred eighty-five kilograms, and a reported weight with fluids of two thousand nine hundred fifty pounds. Normally curb weight already includes fluids, so the lower number should be the dry weight. The page does not explain it. We show both, and we note the inconsistency.
scenes.caption: CURB 3,053 LB (1,385 KG) vs 'WITH FLUIDS' 2,950 LB (1,338 KG) — INCONSISTENT AS LISTED (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: The Drive describes the car as weighing under three thousand pounds, reaching one hundred twenty-four miles per hour from a standstill in four point seven seconds, with a carbon fibre chassis and body. And evo says the F5 weighs twenty-five percent less than the Lamborghini Revuelto, which has about half the F5's power and torque. That is evo's comparison, not ours, and it shows what the weight savings mean in practice.
scenes.query: Hennessey Venom F5 weight and speed
scenes.caption: UNDER 3,000 LB · 0–124 MPH IN 4.7 s (THE DRIVE) · '25% LIGHTER THAN A REVUELTO' (EVO)

scenes.text: To understand the F5, look at its predecessor. Wikipedia lists the Venom GT with a twin-turbo engine rated at one thousand two hundred forty-four horsepower and eleven hundred fifty-five pound-feet of torque, with adjustable settings of eight hundred, one thousand and twelve hundred horsepower. The Spyder open-top version is listed at one thousand four hundred fifty-one horsepower, from the sixteen figures.
scenes.caption: VENOM GT: 1,244 HP / 1,155 LB-FT · SETTINGS 800 / 1,000 / 1,200 HP · SPYDER 1,451 HP (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the F5's headline eighteen seventeen is about forty-six percent more than the Venom GT's twelve forty-four. The Venom GT's recorded speeds climbed as the car developed: Wikipedia lists a Guinness record for zero to three hundred kilometres per hour of thirteen point six three seconds in January twenty thirteen, and two hundred sixty-five point seven miles per hour over two miles in April twenty thirteen.
scenes.caption: 0–300 KM/H IN 13.63 s (JAN 2013) · 265.7 MPH OVER 2 MILES (APR 2013) · F5 HEADLINE POWER +46% vs GT (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Then the two hundred seventy point four nine miles per hour in February twenty fourteen, and, for the Spyder, two hundred sixty-five point five seven miles per hour at Naval Air Station Lemoore on the twenty-fifth of March, twenty sixteen. These are Wikipedia's dates and speeds. By our arithmetic, the Spyder's run was about five miles per hour slower than the coupé's best, and the coupé's best was the one the record body did not accept.
scenes.caption: SPYDER: 265.57 MPH AT NAS LEMOORE, MARCH 25, 2016 · COUPÉ: 270.49 MPH · GAP 4.92 MPH (WIKIPEDIA, OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The Venom GT's production count is unclear, and Wikipedia says so. The overview lists eight units, seven production cars plus a prototype. Hennessey's earlier figure was thirteen vehicles, and a twenty fourteen statement said production would be limited to twenty-nine cars. The page treats thirteen as a planning figure. So the same car has three different counts in the record, which is a warning about production numbers in general.
scenes.caption: VENOM GT UNITS: 8 (7 + PROTOTYPE) · 13 (EARLIER FIGURE) · 29 (2014 STATEMENT) (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: The prices tell their own story. Wikipedia says the Venom GT World's Fastest Edition sold for one point two five million dollars, and that the Steven Tyler Spyder later sold at auction for eight hundred thousand. By our arithmetic, the F5's first-batch price of one point six million dollars is twenty-eight percent above the GT's, and the second batch at two point one is sixty-eight percent above.
scenes.caption: GT WORLD'S FASTEST EDITION $1.25M · TYLER SPYDER $800K AT AUCTION · F5 $1.6M = +28% · $2.1M = +68% (WIKIPEDIA, OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Evo adds a surprise about timing. It says development of the F5 began in twenty twenty-one, while Wikipedia says the car was unveiled as a mock-up in twenty seventeen and first revealed in August twenty fourteen. These are not contradictions if you read them as different stages, concept, engineering and production, but the sources do not explain the stages. We note the gap, rather than guess.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: FIRST REVEALED AUG 2014 · MOCK-UP NOV 2017 · evo: DEVELOPMENT BEGAN 2021 — STAGES NOT EXPLAINED

scenes.text: Customers bought it before it had proved itself. Evo says customers ordered the car before it had reached three hundred miles per hour. Wikipedia says all twenty-four were sold by August twenty twenty-one, which is before any of the test runs we listed. By our arithmetic, that means the cars sold out about three years before the half-mile record of July twenty twenty-four. The buyers bet on the promise.
scenes.caption: ALL 24 SOLD AUG 2021 · HALF-MILE RECORD JULY 2024 ≈ 3 YEARS LATER (WIKIPEDIA, OUR ARITHMETIC) · evo: ORDERED BEFORE REACHING 300 MPH

scenes.text: Hennessey's stated aims, in evo's words, are topping three hundred miles per hour and beating Bugatti with a two-way average, with five hundred kilometres per hour as a stretch target. By our arithmetic, five hundred kilometres per hour is three hundred ten point seven miles per hour, which matches the three hundred eleven that Wikipedia rounds to. A two-way average matters because it cancels out wind.
scenes.query: Hennessey Venom F5 top speed aim
scenes.caption: 500 KM/H = 310.7 MPH (OUR ARITHMETIC) · AIM: 300+ MPH TWO-WAY AVERAGE, BEATING BUGATTI (evo)

scenes.text: The F5 is a rear mid-engine, rear-wheel-drive car with butterfly doors, according to Wikipedia, in coupé and roadster form. Its chassis and body are almost entirely carbon fibre. The dimensions are a wheelbase of one hundred ten point two inches, length one hundred eighty-three point seven, width seventy-seven point one, and height forty-four point five. By our arithmetic, that is a car under four feet tall.
scenes.caption: WHEELBASE 110.2 IN · LENGTH 183.7 · WIDTH 77.1 · HEIGHT 44.5 (≈ 3.7 FT, UNDER 4) (WIKIPEDIA, OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The transmission is a seven-speed CIMA single-clutch automated manual with paddle shifters, according to Wikipedia. The F5-M Roadster and the Revolution LF use a six-speed gated manual instead. The Revolution LF is a one-of-one edition made by Maverick, Hennessey's own division. So even among twenty-four cars, the sources record a manual gearbox in a hypercar that makes over eighteen hundred horsepower.
scenes.caption: 7-SPEED CIMA AUTOMATED MANUAL · F5-M ROADSTER AND REVOLUTION LF: 6-SPEED GATED MANUAL (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: The Revolution was led by Hennessey's chief engineer, John Heinricy, nicknamed Heinrocket, Wikipedia says. It is limited to thirty-six units, twenty-four coupés and twelve roadsters. By our arithmetic, that is one and a half Revolutions for each original F5. The wording is the page's, but the maths is ours, and it says the family has grown past the original promise of twenty-four.
scenes.caption: REVOLUTION LED BY JOHN HEINRICY (WIKIPEDIA) · 36 vs 24 = 1.5× THE ORIGINAL RUN (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Evo also gives a revealing number about the Evolution's acceleration. One hundred to two hundred miles per hour in six point four eight seconds. Compare Wikipedia's claimed zero to two hundred time of ten point three seconds. By our arithmetic, that would leave about three point eight two seconds for zero to one hundred, but the sources are different cars and different claims, so please do not treat that as a measurement.
scenes.caption: 100–200 MPH 6.48 s (evo) · 0–200 MPH CLAIMED 10.3 s (WIKIPEDIA) · IMPLIED 0–100 ≈ 3.82 s — NOT A MEASUREMENT (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Now the thing sitting behind both secrets. The F5 was built to exceed three hundred eleven miles per hour, and as of the sources we read, it has not been shown to do it. Evo, in June twenty twenty-five, says the car had not yet reached that speed, that everyone believes it will get there, and that it cannot be rushed. It ends: just how fast is anyone's guess.
scenes.caption: AS OF evo, JUNE 2025: 300 MPH NOT YET REACHED · 'JUST HOW FAST IS ANYONE'S GUESS'
scenes.chapter: The third thing: the speed it has not shown

scenes.text: What has been shown? Motor One, in a twenty twenty-two article, says the Venom F5 reached two hundred seventy-one point six miles per hour at the Kennedy Space Center in February of that year. Wikipedia lists a half mile in fourteen point four four seconds at two hundred nineteen miles per hour, a production car record, driven by John Hennessey on the thirtieth of July, twenty twenty-four.
scenes.caption: 271.6 MPH (FEB 2022, MOTOR1) · 1/2 MILE: 14.44 s AT 219 MPH, JULY 30, 2024 (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: Evo gives different half-mile numbers from an earlier run on Pilot Sport Cup Two tyres: fourteen point five one seconds at two hundred twenty-one point nine two miles per hour. So two sources list a half mile at about two hundred nineteen and two hundred twenty-two. They may be different runs. By our arithmetic, the time difference is seven hundredths of a second, so the cars are consistent, but the speeds are not.
scenes.caption: evo: 14.51 s AT 221.92 MPH · WIKIPEDIA: 14.44 s AT 219 MPH · TIME GAP 0.07 s, SPEED GAP ~3 MPH (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Evo also gives a standing quarter mile in nine point five seconds at one hundred seventy-three, and one hundred to two hundred miles per hour in six point four eight seconds. Wikipedia lists a quarter mile of nine point eight two at one hundred sixty-nine, from the July twenty twenty-four run. Again, different runs, different conditions. None of these is a top speed. They are acceleration records, and they matter for how the car feels.
scenes.caption: evo: 1/4 MILE 9.5 s AT 173 MPH · 100–200 MPH IN 6.48 s · WIKIPEDIA: 9.82 s AT 169 MPH

scenes.text: Then the crash. The Drive reports that during a zero to two hundred fifty mile per hour test on a Monday in early July twenty twenty-four, at the Shuttle Landing Facility at NASA's Kennedy Space Center, a downforce issue caused the test driver to lose control. Hennessey said the driver walked away without injury, and that the team would evaluate the aerodynamic data to find the root cause.
scenes.caption: JULY 2024 · KENNEDY SPACE CENTER · 0–250 MPH TEST · DOWNFORCE ISSUE · DRIVER UNINJURED (THE DRIVE)

scenes.text: Hennessey did not say which F5 model was tested, The Drive notes. And we do not know the car's fate beyond what Hennessey said. But the crash was on a new aerodynamic setup, which fits what evo says about the car being very sensitive on the nose while the aero changes were still being worked through, a warning from test driver David Donohue that evo reports.
scenes.caption: MODEL TESTED NOT STATED (THE DRIVE) · DONOHUE: CAR SENSITIVE 'ON THE NOSE' DURING AERO CHANGES (EVO)

scenes.text: Evo's Richard Meaden says: it takes less than ten seconds to conclude that the F5 Evolution is my new benchmark. He calls the acceleration brain-scramblingly explosive, but not in the manner of an electric hypercar. Donohue says: this car ruins you for everything else. These are opinions, but they come from two people who actually drove it, which makes them useful evidence of what the car is like.
scenes.query: Hennessey Venom F5 Evolution driving impressions
scenes.caption: MEADEN: 'MY NEW BENCHMARK' · DONOHUE: 'RUINS YOU FOR EVERYTHING ELSE' (EVO)

scenes.text: Production. Wikipedia says the F5 is limited to twenty-four units. Twelve were sold by December twenty twenty at an initial price of one point six million dollars, and the remaining twelve were priced at two point one million. In August twenty twenty-one, the company announced all twenty-four were sold. By our arithmetic, the second twelve cost five hundred thousand dollars more each.
scenes.caption: 24 UNITS · FIRST 12 AT $1.6M · REMAINING 12 AT $2.1M (+$500,000 EACH, OUR ARITHMETIC) · ALL SOLD AUG 2021 (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the full production run at those two prices is twelve times one point six plus twelve times two point one, or forty-four point four million dollars before options. That is our sum from the Wikipedia prices, not a figure any source reports, and real sale prices may differ. It does show the scale of the business: a few dozen cars, each priced like a house.
scenes.caption: 12 × $1.6M + 12 × $2.1M = $44.4M LIST (OUR ARITHMETIC, NOT A REPORTED FIGURE)

scenes.text: The F5 Revolution is a second family. Wikipedia says it is limited to thirty-six units, twenty-four coupés and twelve roadsters, with the roadster allocation sold out, at about two point seven million dollars. The Drive says the Revolution is said to produce more than eight hundred pounds of downforce at one hundred eighty-six miles per hour and more than fourteen hundred pounds at two hundred forty-nine.
scenes.caption: REVOLUTION: 36 UNITS (24 COUPÉ + 12 ROADSTER) · ~$2.7M · >800 LB DOWNFORCE AT 186 MPH · >1,400 LB AT 249 MPH

scenes.text: The design changed on the way to production. Wikipedia says an exterior mock-up shown at SEMA on the first of November, twenty seventeen, had three exhausts and active aerodynamics. Production cars have four exhausts and a smaller fixed spoiler. That matters for the crash story, because active aero is a system that can fail, and a fixed spoiler is not. We note this, but no source ties the two.
scenes.caption: SEMA 2017 MOCK-UP: 3 EXHAUSTS + ACTIVE AERO → PRODUCTION: 4 EXHAUSTS + SMALLER FIXED SPOILER (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: Drag. Wikipedia lists an estimated drag coefficient of zero point three three for the concept, and a claimed zero point three nine for production. By our arithmetic, the production claim is eighteen percent higher than the concept estimate. A higher figure is the usual price of more downforce. It will matter in the next video, when we compare it with the Tuatara's claimed zero point two seven nine.
scenes.caption: Cd 0.33 (CONCEPT ESTIMATE) → 0.39 (PRODUCTION CLAIM) = +18% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · TUATARA CLAIMS 0.279

scenes.text: Is it road legal? The Drive says the production car ships without airbags, and that U.S. buyers get a show-and-display only title. We could not confirm the legal details beyond that article, so we report only what it says. What it means is that the car's ownership rules are different from a normal car's, which affects what a buyer can do with it.
scenes.caption: NO AIRBAGS · U.S. BUYERS GET 'SHOW AND DISPLAY' ONLY (THE DRIVE) · NOT CONFIRMED ELSEWHERE

scenes.text: A note on the Revolution's downforce figures, as reported by The Drive: more than eight hundred pounds at one hundred eighty-six miles per hour, and more than fourteen hundred at two hundred forty-nine. Downforce normally grows with the square of speed. By our arithmetic, two hundred forty-nine over one hundred eighty-six is one point three four, squared is one point seven nine, and eight hundred times that is about fourteen hundred thirty. The two figures agree.
scenes.caption: 800 LB × (249 ÷ 186)² ≈ 1,434 LB vs REPORTED >1,400 LB — CONSISTENT (OUR ARITHMETIC, STANDARD SQUARE-LAW ASSUMPTION)

scenes.text: Speeds in kilometres per hour, for viewers outside the United States. Wikipedia gives the Venom GT's two hundred seventy point four nine miles per hour as four hundred thirty-five point three one kilometres per hour. Motor One gives the F5's two hundred seventy-one point six as four hundred thirty-seven point one. By our arithmetic, the F5's best published speed is one point one miles per hour, or about one point eight kilometres per hour, above the Venom GT's.
scenes.caption: VENOM GT 270.49 MPH = 435.31 KM/H · F5 271.6 MPH = 437.1 KM/H · GAP 1.11 MPH ≈ 1.8 KM/H (WIKIPEDIA, MOTOR1, OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: So the F5's best published top speed is barely above the car it replaced, which ran its record in twenty fourteen. That is not a criticism of the car. Different runs have different lengths of road, and Motor One does not say how long the February twenty-two run had. It is a reminder that a top speed depends on the runway as much as on the engine, a point we return to in the next video.
scenes.query: Hennessey Venom F5 and the runway
scenes.caption: F5 271.6 MPH (2022) vs VENOM GT 270.49 MPH (2014) · RUNWAY LENGTH FOR THE F5 RUN: NOT STATED (MOTOR1)

scenes.text: If you read a hypercar claim, here are four questions this video suggests. Is it a measured speed or a target? Is it one direction or a two-way average? Which fuel was used? And how many cars were built, by whose count? The Venom GT failed the record test on two of those, and the F5 so far has not published the answer to the first. They are fair questions for every car in this series.
scenes.query: How to read a hypercar claim
scenes.caption: FOUR QUESTIONS: MEASURED OR TARGET? ONE-WAY OR TWO-WAY? WHICH FUEL? WHOSE COUNT?

scenes.text: What we could not find. A verified top speed above three hundred miles per hour. The number of F5s delivered to customers, because evo says only that cars are being built and delivered, without a count. The fuel behind the headline power figure. The cost of ownership. And whether the crashed car was repaired. We will not guess any of them.
scenes.caption: NOT IN OUR SOURCES: VERIFIED 300+ MPH · DELIVERY COUNT · FUEL FOR 1,817 HP · OWNERSHIP COSTS · CRASHED CAR'S FATE
scenes.chapter: What our sources do not say

scenes.text: So the two secrets stand. The name comes from the top of the tornado scale, and the headline horsepower is only one of several, depending on fuel. The third thing, the speed, is still a promise. If you are watching in the future and a verified top speed has been published, tell us the source in the comments, and we will update the description with a link.
scenes.caption: NAME = FUJITA SCALE · POWER DEPENDS ON FUEL · TOP SPEED STILL A PROMISE

scenes.text: Which would you rather own, the F5 or its rival the Tuatara? Tell us in the comments. The next videos in this series compare the two cars, count what an American hypercar really costs, and tell the story of America's speed record war. Our twenty twenty-seven Truck Buyer's Guide is linked in the description. Subscribe to Pickup Reality.
scenes.caption: SUBSCRIBE: PICKUP REALITY
